skill.name: set-up-shopware-google-ads-returning-customer-bidding
skill.description: Set up Google Ads returning customer bidding for a Shopware sales channel through Product Metrics. Check whether paid orders are classified correctly, then choose repeat-order revenue or profit as the campaign's bidding signal.
skill.summary: Check Shopware repeat-order tracking and choose a Google Ads bidding goal with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most alerts match Markdown formatting, setup documentation, or scoped account checks. The unpinned installer, missing write approval, broad fallback setup, secret handling, and mutable remote instructions introduce real risks. No evidence of malicious reconnaissance or prompt injection was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Pin the package version and immutable skill source revision. Show the source and require separate approval before executing the installer.

remediation.issue: Setup writes lack an explicit approval rule
remediation.suggestion: Preview the exact workspace, sales channel, ad account, and proposed changes. Require approval before setup writes and check scope again before retrying.

remediation.issue: Fallback setup can expand beyond Google Ads
remediation.suggestion: Give this skill a Google Ads only setup path. Treat other ad channels, Customer Match, and Enhanced Conversions as separate choices with explicit approval.

remediation.issue: Unrelated credentials can pass through the assistant
remediation.suggestion: Remove the credential exceptions from this workflow. Direct users to trusted vendor authorization screens and keep secrets out of chat, tool arguments, and logs.

remediation.issue: Live documentation can replace reviewed instructions
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed references or pin their revision. Treat live documentation as informational and do not let it authorize new actions or data access.

semantic_findings.title: Setup writes lack explicit user approval
semantic_findings.description: The workflow directs the agent to perform Product Metrics setup and retry failed writes without requiring approval for each proposed change. The manual Google Ads goal change does not cover earlier setup writes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The rules explicitly reserve goal changes for the user and require an explicit request for deletes. The general write rules address retries and idempotency, not user approval.

semantic_findings.title: Fallback setup exceeds the requested advertising scope
semantic_findings.description: The Google Ads workflow points to a Shopware checklist that names Meta and ChatGPT Ads as setup steps. Following it without narrowing scope could prompt unnecessary access grants and expose order data to additional destinations.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback lists all three channel connections without marking the other two optional for this task. The user performs the connection steps, so transfer is not automatic.

semantic_findings.title: Unrelated credentials can pass through the assistant
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows the agent to collect and forward credentials for Lightspeed, Meta, and OpenAI. These exceptions are unrelated to Shopware returning customer bidding and do not specify a protected input channel.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The secrets rule explicitly allows these credentials and says to pass them to the command. Its logging prohibition does not establish a protected way to enter them.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable remote documentation can replace reviewed references
semantic_findings.description: When bundled references are unavailable, the skill directs the agent to fetch live vendor pages as replacement workflow instructions. Later edits could alter the actions taken without changing the reviewed skill.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback treats the live pages as equivalent to local references without pinning revisions or verifying content. This is a trust gap, not evidence of malicious page content.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopware Returning Customer Bidding in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A general purchase goal does not distinguish repeat orders from first purchases. Use Product Metrics to check the repeat-order signal and choose a Google Ads goal based on returning customer revenue or profit.
actual_capabilities: Read Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP server and identify incomplete steps.
Guide a store administrator through pairing one Shopware sales channel and linking it to the Google Ads property.
Check recent paid orders for new, returning, or unknown customer classifications.
Guide creation of secondary conversion actions and explain the choice between returning customer revenue and profit.
Read back conversion action status after the user updates their goal in Google Ads.
limitations: The plugin requires Shopware 6.7 and PHP 8.2 or later. Each installation covers one sales channel.
Live checks require access to the relevant Product Metrics workspace. The Google Ads setup also requires linked Merchant Center access.
Profit signals require active additional costs and complete order costs. Consent affects whether conversions are sent.
The user must authorize connections and make primary conversion goal changes in Google Ads.

use_cases.title: Check whether a store is ready
use_cases.description: Find missing connections and tracking steps for one Shopware sales channel before planning a retention campaign.

use_cases.title: Choose a retention campaign goal
use_cases.description: Compare returning customer revenue and profit as bidding signals. Plan the goal change for one campaign first.

use_cases.title: Investigate missing repeat-order conversions
use_cases.description: Check classification, payment status, and consent requirements before comparing store orders with Google Ads results.

prompt_templates.title: Check setup readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Check returning customer bidding readiness for my Shopware sales channel in Product Metrics. Tell me what is ready and what I still need to do. Make no changes.

prompt_templates.title: Review order classifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the last 20 available orders in my paired Shopware sales channel. Summarize the new, returning, and unknown counts without showing customer details.

prompt_templates.title: Compare revenue and profit goals
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the returning customer revenue and profit goals for my Google Ads retention campaign. Check for missing costs and list the settings I would change myself.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a campaign rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Review tracking readiness and goal status after my campaign change. Check a paid test order for returning classification and mark any bidding settings you cannot verify. Do not change any settings.

output_examples.input: Is my connected Shopware channel ready for returning customer bidding?
output: The Shopware channel is active, and both returning customer conversion actions are present as secondary actions.
The profit action is not ready because additional costs are inactive. Keep the current bidding goal until you verify a repeat-order conversion.

output_examples.input: Why did my second paid test order not count as returning?
output: The test order was paid, but the earlier order was in a different sales channel. Product Metrics does not use that order for classification.
Check a test order with an earlier paid purchase in the same channel. Confirm the store's consent settings before checking Google Ads.

best_practices: Verify the workspace, sales channel, and Google Ads account before approving any setup change.
Confirm consent and validate a paid repeat order in the paired channel before switching a campaign goal.
Apply the new goal to one retention campaign first and check that it uses only one primary purchase action.
anti_patterns: Making both the revenue and profit actions primary for the same campaign.
Assuming an order from a different Shopware sales channel counts toward returning customer history.
Pasting a Shopware pairing token or advertising credential into chat.

faq.question: What software does this setup require?
faq.answer: You need Shopware 6.7, PHP 8.2 or later, Product Metrics Pro, and a Google Ads account linked to Merchant Center.

faq.question: How does Product Metrics identify returning customers?
faq.answer: It checks for an earlier paid order in the same sales channel. It matches customer accounts or guest email addresses.

faq.question: Can I use profit instead of revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Activate additional costs and check that order costs are complete before choosing the returning customer profit action.

faq.question: Does the skill change my primary conversion goal?
faq.answer: No. You change the goal in Google Ads. The skill can then check the conversion action status.

faq.question: What if Product Metrics cannot classify an order?
faq.answer: An unknown order does not count toward the new or returning customer action. It may still contribute to general revenue or profit reporting.

faq.question: Can consent affect the conversion count?
faq.answer: Yes. Product Metrics follows the configured consent platform. Confirm the selected banner and verify that the required consent is present for the test order.
